# Running E2E tests

There are two Playwright suites.

| Suite         | Runs against                                  | Command           |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `e2e/`        | A disposable Saleor in docker, seeded locally | `pnpm e2e`        |
| `e2e-legacy/` | A provisioned Saleor Cloud instance           | `pnpm e2e:legacy` |

New tests belong in `e2e/`. See [`e2e/README.md`](../e2e/README.md) — it covers the two
Saleor targets (latest stable and unreleased main), how seeds are built and cached, and how
to port a spec across.

## The legacy suite

> [!NOTE]
> `e2e-legacy/` is frozen. It is kept running until its specs have been reviewed and ported
> to `e2e/`; it should not be extended or edited.

It is based on Saleor Cloud and uses snapshots with prepared data. To run it against your
own infrastructure you need to update the test data with your own created objects in
[`e2e-legacy/data/e2eTestData.ts`](../e2e-legacy/data/e2eTestData.ts) and create a snapshot.

Playwright-specific env variables for `.env`:

```
BASE_URL=
API_URL=

E2E_USER_NAME=
E2E_USER_PASSWORD=
E2E_PERMISSIONS_USERS_PASSWORD=

MAILPITURL=
```

Then:

```shell
pnpm run e2e:legacy
```

If you change `BASE_URL` to run against a different environment, clear the login data cached
in `e2e-legacy/.auth`:

```shell
pnpm run e2e:legacy:clean-auth
```

# Saleor Dashboard

## Conventions

- Use `@saleor/macaw-ui-next` components and tokens; do not add usages of legacy
  `@saleor/macaw-ui`, Material-UI, or `makeStyles`.
- Import icons directly from `lucide-react`; Macaw icons are deprecated.
- Use CSS Modules (`.module.css`) for custom styles.
- Write new code with strict TypeScript checking; do not add `// @ts-strict-ignore`.
- Use named exports and direct imports. Do not introduce barrel exports;
  route entry points named `index.tsx` are allowed.
- Prefer destructured object parameters and typed declarations over type assertions.
  Explicitly type test fixtures.
- Internationalize user-facing text with `react-intl`. Check `src/intl.ts` and nearby
  component messages for reusable messages before defining new ones.
- Add a colocated `ComponentName.stories.tsx` for new UI components.
- In tests, use `// Arrange`, `// Act`, and `// Assert` comments. Mock GraphQL
  operations with typed fixtures.
- For lists that can contain 50+ items, keep navigation and controls usable and
  selected items discoverable. Choose scrolling, pagination, or virtualization to
  suit the component. Use skeletons for loading and handle empty states.

## Task-specific context

Read documentation when its subject is relevant to the task:

- `CONTEXT.md` for product terminology, especially modeling and navigation pins.
  Use its dashboard-facing names even when API names differ.
- Relevant decisions in `docs/adr/` when changing the behavior they govern.
  Surface conflicts with those decisions rather than silently overriding them.
- `docs/multi-schema.md` for GraphQL operations, generation, or schema selection.
- `docs/configuration.md` and `.env.template` when configuring or running the app.
- `docs/running-tests.md` when running Playwright tests.

Read current commands, dependencies, and runtime requirements from `package.json`,
including `packageManager` and `engines`; read aliases from `tsconfig.json`.

## Conditional workflows

- Install dependencies when missing or when dependency inputs change. Run
  `pnpm install` after modifying `package.json` or workspace dependency settings.
- Put dependency overrides in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` under `overrides`, never in
  `package.json` under `pnpm.overrides`.
- After changing GraphQL operations, fragments, or schemas, run `pnpm run generate`
  for both main and staging schemas. Do not hand-edit `.generated.ts` files.
- After changing `react-intl` messages, run `pnpm run extract-messages`.
- Set up a backend only when the task needs a running application or integration
  tests. Setup and code generation are not prerequisites for unrelated edits.
- Run `pnpm run dev` in the background. If background execution is unavailable,
  ask the user how to proceed. Its `predev` hook already runs code generation.

## Verification

Match verification to the affected code. Complete relevant checks before handing
back implementation work, and report any checks that could not run.

- Documentation-only changes: format the changed files with Prettier; application
  tests, type checks, and knip are unnecessary.
- Code changes: run oxlint with auto-fix and Prettier on the changed files before
  manually fixing lint errors. ESLint only runs GraphQL rules
  (`eslint.config.mjs`); run it on changed GraphQL operations. Run affected tests
  and the relevant `check-types:*` scripts from `package.json`.
- Use `pnpm run test:quiet <file_path>` for individual Jest files. Switch to
  `pnpm run test:debug <file_path>` when debugging requires console or DOM output.
- Add or update unit tests for changed utility behavior and complex components;
  use Playwright coverage for critical user flows.
- When changing dependencies, exports, or file organization, run `pnpm run knip`.
- For changes spanning application code, Playwright, and scripts, run
  `pnpm run check-types`. Use `pnpm run lint` for repository-wide lint, formatting,
  and changeset validation; it auto-fixes and formats files across the repository.
- Rerun affected checks after fixes. Broaden verification when shared behavior,
  configuration changes, or failures warrant it; avoid repeating successful checks
  without new changes or evidence.

## Conflict resolution and review

- Resolve source conflicts first, then regenerate derived files:
  `pnpm install` for `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm run generate` for GraphQL outputs.
  Do not manually merge generated content.
- Resolve package-version conflicts against intended dependency constraints and
  preserve deliberate pins. Do not turn conflict resolution into an unrelated
  upgrade to the latest registry release.
- During code review, skip inspecting `.generated.ts` contents; review the source
  operations and generation configuration instead.

## Analytics

- When adding a substantial product feature, implement PostHog tracking for its key
  user interactions and outcomes, following existing analytics patterns.
- Do not add tracking for bug fixes, removals, refactors, or other maintenance-only changes.

## Contributions

- Use the changesets CLI for user-facing features, enhancements, and bug fixes.
  Explain the user-visible behavior; for fixes, describe what failed and what works
  now. Skip changesets for internal refactors, style, tests, CI/CD, and internal docs.
- Follow scope policy in `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md` (Pull requests section) and
  title and description requirements in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`.
- Run the `saleor-dashboard-pr-quality-check` skill when planning (to keep the
  planned scope to one PR) and when work is done, including after each commit.
  Without an open PR it checks the local branch. If it recommends a split, surface
  that to the user before continuing.
- Prefer the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations.
- No agent-driven issue tracker is configured. Return issue or triage findings in
  the conversation; see `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` when a skill expects a tracker.

72	`populatedb` and the GraphQL API — and captured as a `pg_dump --data-only`. Tests never run

76	collections, pages, menus, vouchers, gift cards, orders, customers, promotions, shipping

83	safe. Cached logins share the key, so a rebuilt seed can never be paired with a token minted

92	`test.use({ scenario: "..." })` in the spec. A scenario builds from an empty database, or -
93	with `parent: "default"` - on top of another scenario's dump. Build on `default` unless you

96

98	new products are not searchable, and catalogue promotions do not reach prices, until a
99	periodic task runs. `ensureScenario` therefore runs those tasks after every build, before the
100	dump (`lib/beat.ts`). A scenario that creates something another beat task settles adds that

103	## Isolation, and opting into parallel
104	
105	By default the database is restored **before every test**, and those tests run one at a
106	time. That single property is what the suite is for: a failing test reproduces on its own,
107	rather than as a function of the tests that ran before it. Specs need no cleanup
108	discipline and no unique names, and nothing in the seed is ever consumed.
109	
110	Serial is the default because a restore empties every table for a second or two — a test
111	running alongside one would see a shop with no products and no users in it.
112	
113	A block that leaves nothing behind can opt out of the reset, and then run in parallel:
114	
115	```ts
116	import { parallel } from "../config.ts";
117	
118	test.describe("Catalogue list", { tag: parallel() }, () => { ... });      // default scenario
119	test.describe("Refunds", { tag: parallel("refunded-orders") }, () => { ... });
120	```

122	The tag takes a **scenario name**, so the group and the database state it runs on are the
123	same thing and cannot drift apart. A run is then:
124

126	restore:default          one restore, alone
127	parallel:default         every test tagged parallel(),          all at once

131	```

134	interleaved in declaration order. That is deliberate, and it is also the cheaper
135	arrangement: this costs one restore per group plus one per serial test, where interleaving
136	would add a restore at every boundary and buy nothing — tests are independent by
137	construction, so the order between groups carries no meaning.
138	
139	Playwright's project `dependencies` are what enforce it; they are the only ordering
140	primitive that spans workers, which is also why a group's restore is a project rather than
141	a hook. A scenario with no tagged tests still pays for its restore project (a second or
142	two) — whether a group has members is not knowable when the config is read.

145	context, so the ceiling is memory rather than cores.
146	
147	Because arrangement cannot be done as an admin at test time, **a state a spec needs is a

152	Saleor blocks an IP for a second before _every_ login attempt — deliberately, "to prevent
153	concurrent requests" (`saleor/account/throttling.py`), unconditionally in `tokenCreate`,

185	
186	`e2e-legacy/` is the Cloud-snapshot suite. **It is frozen — do not edit it.** Its results

188	nobody can verify.

199	`this.page`.)

201	## Deferred
202	
203	Real shortcuts, taken knowingly, with what would undo them:
204	
205	- **The serial phase is serial.** One database per worker (`saleor_w0`, `saleor_w1`, …)
206	  restored from the same dump would parallelise the resetting tests too. Do it when serial
207	  run time, not the reseed itself, is what hurts — note it also needs one Saleor API per
208	  database, and the dashboard bundle bakes its `API_URL` at build time.
209	- **Reset per test.** Batch to per-file for specs that demonstrably do not need it — but
210	  only against a measurement, since it trades back the reproducibility above.
211	- **No parallel group has members yet.** `tests/login.spec.ts` cannot be tagged (above).
212	  The first ported spec that reads without writing should be.
213	- **Only the superuser signs in through the UI.** The flow is shared code for every user,
214	  so the other actors are covered by global setup signing them in over the API.
215	- **A full `vite build` per target.** Currently skipped only when the fingerprint of `src/`,
216	  `locale/`, `.featureFlags/`, `vite.config.js` and `package.json` is unchanged. A finer
217	  fingerprint, or a shared build cache in CI, would cut a cold run substantially.
218	- **`nginx/replace-env-vars.sh` is not exercised.** The bundle is mounted read-only and its
219	  environment is baked at build time (it has to be, for the schema flag). The shipped
220	  image's runtime substitution therefore has no coverage here; it wants a smoke test of the
221	  actual Docker image, which is a different suite.
222	- **Nightly CI only.** `.github/workflows/e2e-local.yml` runs nightly and on demand. A
223	  failed nightly run posts its failed tests to Slack; a manual run does not.
224	  Putting it on pull requests is a one-line change once the suite is broad enough to be
225	  worth the minutes.
226	- **Few specs so far.** `tests/login.spec.ts` and the order flows in `tests/orders/`. A
227	  single-permission spec is still worth porting early — it is the part of the actor model
228	  most likely to be subtly wrong, and the first place a `populatedb` difference between
229	  `3.23` and `unstable-main` would show.
230	- **No multi-actor test helper.** One actor per test. Two actors in one test needs a second
231	  `browser.newContext({ storageState })`; four lines, written when a spec needs it.
232	- **Product images are skipped** (`populatedb --withoutimages`) — minutes off the build and
233	  megabytes off every restore. A spec asserting on media needs its own scenario.

1	import { defineConfig, devices } from "@playwright/test";
2	
3	import { e2eConfig, PARALLEL_TAG_PATTERN, parallel } from "./config.ts";
4	import { SCENARIOS } from "./scenarios/registry.ts";
5	
6	const config = e2eConfig();
7	
8	/**
9	 * Phases, sequenced by Playwright's project `dependencies` - the only ordering primitive
10	 * that spans workers.
11	 *
12	 * For each scenario, in registry order:
13	 *
14	 *   restore:<scenario>  one restore, alone
15	 *   parallel:<scenario> every test tagged `parallel("<scenario>")`, all at once
16	 *
17	 * then, once every group has finished:
18	 *
19	 *   <target>            everything untagged, one test at a time, each from its own reset
20	 *
21	 * Groups run one after another rather than interleaved with the serial tests, and that is
22	 * deliberate: a reset empties the tables for a second or two, so nothing may overlap it.
23	 * Batching every parallel group ahead of the serial phase also costs the *fewest* restores
24	 * - one per group, plus one per serial test. Interleaving by declaration order would add a
25	 * restore at each boundary and buy nothing, since tests are independent by construction.
26	 *
27	 * A scenario with no tagged tests still pays for its restore project (a second or two).
28	 * Whether a group has members is not knowable when this config is read.
29	 */
30	const buildProjects = () => {
31	  const browser = { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"] };
32	  const projects = [];
33	  let previous: string[] = [];
34	
35	  for (const scenario of Object.keys(SCENARIOS)) {
36	    const restore = `restore:${scenario}`;
37	    const group = `parallel:${scenario}`;
38	
39	    projects.push({
40	      name: restore,
41	      testDir: "./setup",
42	      testMatch: /.*\.setup\.ts/,
43	      dependencies: previous,
44	      use: { ...browser, scenario },
45	    });
46	    projects.push({
47	      name: group,
48	      grep: new RegExp(parallel(scenario)),
49	      fullyParallel: true,
50	      dependencies: [restore],
51	      use: { ...browser, scenario },
52	    });
53	
54	    previous = [group];
55	  }
56	
57	  projects.push({
58	    name: config.target,
59	    grepInvert: PARALLEL_TAG_PATTERN,
60	    /* A reset cannot share a moment with another test. */
61	    workers: 1,
62	    dependencies: previous,
63	    use: browser,
64	  });
65	
66	  return projects;
67	};
68	
69	export default defineConfig({
70	  testDir: "./tests",
71	  /*
72	   * Set explicitly: left to the default this resolves against the nearest package.json and
73	   * lands at the repository root, next to the legacy suite's output.
74	   */
75	  outputDir: "./test-results",
76	  globalSetup: "./global-setup.ts",
77	  /*
78	   * The ceiling for the whole run; each project takes what it needs from it below. Each
79	   * parallel test is a browser context, so the useful bound is memory, not cores.
80	   */
81	  workers: Number(process.env.E2E_WORKERS) || 4,
82	  fullyParallel: false,
83	  forbidOnly: Boolean(process.env.CI),
84	  /*
85	   * No retries. A per-test reseed means a failure is reproducible on its own, so a retry
86	   * mostly hides a real defect behind a second attempt.
87	   */
88	  retries: 0,
89	  timeout: 60_000,
90	  expect: { timeout: 15_000 },
91	  /*
92	   * The html report is what the CI workflow uploads as an artifact; `github` annotates the
93	   * run; the json one is what the nightly Slack message lists failed tests from.
94	   */
95	  reporter: process.env.CI
96	    ? [
97	        ["github"],
98	        ["list"],
99	        ["html", { open: "never" }],
100	        ["json", { outputFile: "test-results/results.json" }],
101	      ]
102	    : [["html", { open: "never" }], ["list"]],
103	  use: {
104	    baseURL: config.dashboardUrl,
105	    testIdAttribute: "data-test-id",
106	    /*
107	     * Without this a click on a locator that never matches waits out the whole test budget
108	     * in silence, which reads exactly like a slow page rather than a wrong selector.
109	     */
110	    actionTimeout: 15_000,
111	    trace: process.env.CI ? "retain-on-failure" : "on",
112	    screenshot: "only-on-failure",
113	    video: process.env.CI ? "retain-on-failure" : "off",
114	  },
115	  projects: buildProjects(),
116	});

1	/**
2	 * Every value the suite needs that depends on which Saleor it is running against.
3	 *
4	 * The dashboard supports two API generations at once: the latest stable release and
5	 * Saleor's unreleased main branch, selected at *build time* by FF_USE_STAGING_SCHEMA
6	 * (see vite.config.js - it lands in `define`, so the inactive schema tree is dropped
7	 * from the bundle). A target is therefore a Saleor image *and* a dashboard build; the
8	 * two cannot be mixed at runtime.
9	 *
10	 * One target runs at a time. Ports differ per target anyway so a leftover stack from
11	 * the other one cannot answer by accident.
12	 */
13	export type Target = "stable" | "main";
14	
15	export const TARGETS: Target[] = ["stable", "main"];
16	
17	const isTarget = (value: string): value is Target => TARGETS.includes(value as Target);
18	
19	interface TargetConfig {
20	  /**
21	   * Floating on purpose: `3.23` tracks the latest patch of the stable line, so a Saleor
22	   * bugfix release is picked up by the next `--fresh` run instead of by a version-bump PR.
23	   * `unstable-main` is the image Saleor publishes from its main branch.
24	   *
25	   * When Saleor releases 3.24, this is the one line to change: stable becomes `3.24`.
26	   */
27	  image: string;
28	  /** Build the dashboard against the staging (unreleased) GraphQL schema. */
29	  stagingSchema: boolean;
30	  apiPort: number;
31	  dashboardPort: number;
32	}
33	
34	const TARGET_CONFIG: Record<Target, TargetConfig> = {
35	  stable: { image: "3.23", stagingSchema: false, apiPort: 8200, dashboardPort: 9200 },
36	  main: { image: "unstable-main", stagingSchema: true, apiPort: 8300, dashboardPort: 9300 },
37	};
38	
39	/**
40	 * The admin the suite drives the API with. Created by `populatedb --createsuperuser`,
41	 * so the password is a constant rather than a secret - the stack is local and disposable.
42	 */
43	export const ADMIN = { email: "admin@example.com", password: "admin" };
44	
45	/** Every staff user `populatedb` mints gets this password (`--staff_password`). */
46	export const STAFF_PASSWORD = "password";
47	
48	/**
49	 * Opts a block into the parallel phase for a scenario: `{ tag: parallel() }` on a
50	 * `describe`, or on a single test. Untagged is the default and means serial.
51	 *
52	 * A tagged test gets no reset of its own. Its whole group shares one database, restored
53	 * once before the group starts, so every test in it must leave nothing behind that another
54	 * test in the group - or a later one - could notice.
55	 *
56	 * The argument names the database state the group runs on, which is a scenario, so the
57	 * group and the scenario are the same thing and cannot disagree.
58	 *
59	 * Tests tagged for the same scenario are one group however far apart they are written, so
60	 * seven tests - 1-3 tagged, 4 untagged, 5-7 tagged - run as:
61	 *
62	 *   restore, then 1 2 3 5 6 7 together   <- one group, one restore
63	 *   restore, then 4                      <- serial, its own restore
64	 *
65	 * Two restores. The tagged tests do not run in two sittings around test 4, because the
66	 * order between independent tests carries no meaning and splitting them would cost a third
67	 * restore for nothing. What is guaranteed is the part that matters: a serial test never
68	 * overlaps a parallel one, and never shares a database with anything.
69	 *
70	 * Tagging 5-7 as `parallel("other")` instead does split them - into a second group with a
71	 * second restore, because they asked for a different database state. Groups run one after
72	 * another, each after its own restore; ungrouped tests run last, one at a time.
73	 */
74	export const parallel = (scenario = "default"): string => `@parallel:${scenario}`;
75	
76	/** Matches any parallel tag - used to route the remaining tests to the serial phase. */
77	export const PARALLEL_TAG_PATTERN = /@parallel:/;
78	
79	/**
80	 * The single place a target name is validated. `run.ts` puts `--target` into the environment
81	 * rather than parsing it itself, so a typo is rejected the same way from either direction.
82	 */
83	export const targetFromEnv = (): Target => {
84	  const value = process.env.E2E_TARGET ?? "stable";
85	
86	  if (!isTarget(value)) {
87	    throw new Error(`target must be one of ${TARGETS.join(", ")} - got "${value}"`);
88	  }
89	
90	  return value;
91	};
92	
93	export const e2eConfig = (target: Target = targetFromEnv()) => {
94	  const { image, stagingSchema, apiPort, dashboardPort } = TARGET_CONFIG[target];
95	
96	  return {
97	    target,
98	    image: `ghcr.io/saleor/saleor:${image}`,
99	    stagingSchema,
100	    /** Compose project name - keeps the two targets' containers and volumes apart. */
101	    projectName: `dashboard-e2e-${target}`,
102	    apiPort,
103	    dashboardPort,
104	    apiUrl: `http://localhost:${apiPort}/graphql/`,
105	    dashboardUrl: `http://localhost:${dashboardPort}/`,
106	    /** Kept out of `build/` so a running `pnpm dev` is unaffected by a suite run. */
107	    buildDir: `build-e2e-${target}`,
108	  };
109	};
110	
111	export type E2eConfig = ReturnType<typeof e2eConfig>;

12	 * behind) - the dump captures both the same way, but SQL is the thing that rots when
13	 * Saleor's tables change, and this suite deliberately tracks a floating image.

19	   * build starting from an empty database. Besides saving the parent's build, that keeps
20	   * the parent's rows - the staff users above all, whose cached sessions are only valid
21	   * against the rows they were minted for - identical in both dumps.
22	   */

2	import { manage } from "./docker.ts";

4	/**
5	 * Work Saleor defers to Celery beat. Mutations only flag rows as dirty; a periodic task
6	 * picks them up later. This stack runs a worker but no beat, so without these a scenario's
7	 * dump would capture the flags and never the result.
8	 *
9	 * `CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER` is no substitute: it runs tasks something enqueues, and
10	 * nothing enqueues these - only the beat schedule does (`CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE` in Saleor's
11	 * `settings.py`). `populatedb` calls the promotion ones directly for the same reason.
12	 *
13	 * Add a task here when a scenario creates something another beat task settles.
14	 */
15	const BEAT_TASKS = [
16	  // Product search index - the dashboard's product pickers find nothing new without it.
17	  "saleor.product.tasks.update_products_search_vector_task",
18	  // Catalogue promotions reach prices in two passes: variants linked to rules, then
19	  // discounted prices recomputed.
20	  "saleor.product.tasks.update_variant_relations_for_active_promotion_rules_task",
21	  "saleor.product.tasks.recalculate_discounted_price_for_products_task",
22	];
23	
24	/**
25	 * Each task handles one batch per call, so the list runs a few rounds - more than a
26	 * scenario's handful of rows needs. A task with nothing left to do is a no-op.
27	 */
28	const ROUNDS = 3;
29	
30	/** Runs every beat task in `BEAT_TASKS` to completion, synchronously, in one container. */
31	export const runBeatTasks = (config: E2eConfig) =>
32	  manage(config, [
33	    "shell",
34	    "-c",
35	    [
36	      "from importlib import import_module",
37	      `for _ in range(${ROUNDS}):`,
38	      `    for path in ${JSON.stringify(BEAT_TASKS)}:`,
39	      "        module, name = path.rsplit('.', 1)",
40	      "        getattr(import_module(module), name)()",
41	    ].join("\n"),
42	  ]);

{
  "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/tsconfig.json",
  // Standalone config for the local-stack E2E suite. The orchestration scripts
  // (`run.ts`, `lib/`, `scenarios/`) are executed directly by Node's TypeScript
  // type stripping (Node >= 24), so relative imports keep their `.ts` extension.
  // Playwright compiles `tests/` and `pages/` itself and resolves the aliases below.
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "module": "esnext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "target": "esnext",
    // Page objects initialize their locators as class fields from `constructor(readonly
    // page: Page) {}`. That needs the parameter property assigned before the fields, which
    // is how Playwright's own transform runs them; `esnext` alone would imply the opposite.
    "useDefineForClassFields": false,
    "lib": ["esnext", "dom"],
    "types": ["node"],
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true
  },
  "include": ["**/*.ts"]
}
# The local-stack E2E suite: a disposable Saleor in docker, the dashboard built from this
# branch, no Saleor Cloud involved.
#
# Nightly and on demand. The suite is young, and a full run is dominated by a `vite build`
# per target; putting it on every pull request before it has earned the time would mostly
# buy queue. Moving it onto pull requests is a one-line change to the `on:` block.
name: E2E (local stack)

on:
  # Nightly against both targets. `unstable-main` moves daily, so this is also what notices
  # a Saleor change that breaks the dashboard before a release does.
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 3 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      target:
        type: choice
        description: "Which Saleor to test against"
        required: false
        default: "both"
        options:
          - both
          - stable
          - main
      grep:
        type: string
        description: "Playwright --grep filter (optional)"
        required: false

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions: {}

jobs:
  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 60

    strategy:
      # The targets are independent; a break in one is worth seeing alongside the other.
      fail-fast: false
      # Anything other than a single named target - "both", or a scheduled run, which has no
      # inputs at all - means run them both.
      matrix:
        target: ${{ fromJSON((inputs.target == 'stable' || inputs.target == 'main') &&
          format('["{0}"]', inputs.target) || '["stable","main"]') }}

    permissions:
      contents: read

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413 # v6.1.0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0

  creates something that a beat task settles, add that task to `e2e/lib/beat.ts`.

# Saleor Dashboard

## Conventions

- Use `@saleor/macaw-ui-next` components and tokens; do not add usages of legacy
  `@saleor/macaw-ui`, Material-UI, or `makeStyles`.
- Import icons directly from `lucide-react`; Macaw icons are deprecated.
- Use CSS Modules (`.module.css`) for custom styles.
- Write new code with strict TypeScript checking; do not add `// @ts-strict-ignore`.
- Use named exports and direct imports. Do not introduce barrel exports;
  route entry points named `index.tsx` are allowed.
- Prefer destructured object parameters and typed declarations over type assertions.
  Explicitly type test fixtures.
- Internationalize user-facing text with `react-intl`. Check `src/intl.ts` and nearby
  component messages for reusable messages before defining new ones.
- Add a colocated `ComponentName.stories.tsx` for new UI components.
- In tests, use `// Arrange`, `// Act`, and `// Assert` comments. Mock GraphQL
  operations with typed fixtures.
- For lists that can contain 50+ items, keep navigation and controls usable and
  selected items discoverable. Choose scrolling, pagination, or virtualization to
  suit the component. Use skeletons for loading and handle empty states.

## Task-specific context

Read documentation when its subject is relevant to the task:

- `CONTEXT.md` for product terminology, especially modeling and navigation pins.
  Use its dashboard-facing names even when API names differ.
- Relevant decisions in `docs/adr/` when changing the behavior they govern.
  Surface conflicts with those decisions rather than silently overriding them.
- `docs/multi-schema.md` for GraphQL operations, generation, or schema selection.
- `docs/configuration.md` and `.env.template` when configuring or running the app.
- `docs/running-tests.md` when running Playwright tests.

Read current commands, dependencies, and runtime requirements from `package.json`,
including `packageManager` and `engines`; read aliases from `tsconfig.json`.

## Conditional workflows

- Install dependencies when missing or when dependency inputs change. Run
  `pnpm install` after modifying `package.json` or workspace dependency settings.
- Put dependency overrides in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` under `overrides`, never in
  `package.json` under `pnpm.overrides`.
- After changing GraphQL operations, fragments, or schemas, run `pnpm run generate`
  for both main and staging schemas. Do not hand-edit `.generated.ts` files.
- After changing `react-intl` messages, run `pnpm run extract-messages`.
- Set up a backend only when the task needs a running application or integration
  tests. Setup and code generation are not prerequisites for unrelated edits.
- Run `pnpm run dev` in the background. If background execution is unavailable,
  ask the user how to proceed. Its `predev` hook already runs code generation.

## Verification

Match verification to the affected code. Complete relevant checks before handing
back implementation work, and report any checks that could not run.

- Documentation-only changes: format the changed files with Prettier; application
  tests, type checks, and knip are unnecessary.
- Code changes: run oxlint with auto-fix and Prettier on the changed files before
  manually fixing lint errors. ESLint only runs GraphQL rules
  (`eslint.config.mjs`); run it on changed GraphQL operations. Run affected tests
  and the relevant `check-types:*` scripts from `package.json`.
- Use `pnpm run test:quiet <file_path>` for individual Jest files. Switch to
  `pnpm run test:debug <file_path>` when debugging requires console or DOM output.
- Add or update unit tests for changed utility behavior and complex components;
  use Playwright coverage for critical user flows.
- When changing dependencies, exports, or file organization, run `pnpm run knip`.
- For changes spanning application code, Playwright, and scripts, run
  `pnpm run check-types`. Use `pnpm run lint` for repository-wide lint, formatting,
  and changeset validation; it auto-fixes and formats files across the repository.
- Rerun affected checks after fixes. Broaden verification when shared behavior,
  configuration changes, or failures warrant it; avoid repeating successful checks
  without new changes or evidence.

## Conflict resolution and review

- Resolve source conflicts first, then regenerate derived files:
  `pnpm install` for `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm run generate` for GraphQL outputs.
  Do not manually merge generated content.
- Resolve package-version conflicts against intended dependency constraints and
  preserve deliberate pins. Do not turn conflict resolution into an unrelated
  upgrade to the latest registry release.
- During code review, skip inspecting `.generated.ts` contents; review the source
  operations and generation configuration instead.

## Analytics

- When adding a substantial product feature, implement PostHog tracking for its key
  user interactions and outcomes, following existing analytics patterns.
- Do not add tracking for bug fixes, removals, refactors, or other maintenance-only changes.

## Contributions

- Use the changesets CLI for user-facing features, enhancements, and bug fixes.
  Explain the user-visible behavior; for fixes, describe what failed and what works
  now. Skip changesets for internal refactors, style, tests, CI/CD, and internal docs.
- Follow scope policy in `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md` (Pull requests section) and
  title and description requirements in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`.
- Run the `saleor-dashboard-pr-quality-check` skill when planning (to keep the
  planned scope to one PR) and when work is done, including after each commit.
  Without an open PR it checks the local branch. If it recommends a split, surface
  that to the user before continuing.
- Prefer the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations.
- No agent-driven issue tracker is configured. Return issue or triage findings in
  the conversation; see `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` when a skill expects a tracker.

I added an "End-to-end tests" section to `AGENTS.md`, just before "Conflict resolution and review". `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md`, so both pick it up. Prettier did not run: the command needed approval and this session can't grant it. Please run `pnpm exec prettier --write AGENTS.md`.

I based the rules on the whole `e2e/` suite (6 specs, page objects, scenarios, fixtures, config, `e2e/README.md`, the nightly CI workflow). The main ones:

- **Where tests go:** new specs belong in `e2e/`. `e2e-legacy/` is frozen. A spec that replaces legacy tests names the `SALEOR_<n>` cases it covers.
- **Test data:** each test starts from a freshly restored database. Data a spec needs is set up as a named scenario, not created inside the test. Scenarios build on `parent: "default"`, use the GraphQL API, and check every mutation for errors.
- **IDs:** never hard-coded, because they change on every rebuild. Specs look them up at test time with read-only queries, the way `findOrderId` does.
- **Signed-in user:** chosen per spec with `test.use({ actor })`. The single-permission users cover permission flows.
- **Parallel runs:** tests run one at a time unless tagged `parallel()`. A tagged test must leave nothing behind and must not sign in. That includes the `signIn`, `adminToken` and `findOrderId` helpers, because Saleor throttles logins by IP. The README only mentions UI logins, but the throttle sits in `tokenCreate` itself.
- **Saleor versions:** tests run against both stable and unreleased main. A feature that exists on only one is skipped with `test.skip(config.stagingSchema, …)`.
- **Code style:** page objects use `readonly` locator fields and an empty constructor. Locators use `data-test-id` or roles. No `waitForTimeout`, `force`, `nth`, retries or raised timeouts. External services are intercepted with `page.route`.

The existing specs don't all follow these rules, so a reviewer would hit this on day one:

- **`e2e/scenarios/productMediaTranslations.ts`** restores the default scenario by hand instead of setting `parent: "default"`, which is what the README asks for.
- **`productMediaTranslations.spec.ts`** and **`feedback.spec.ts`** use raw locators in the test bodies and no page objects. `feedback.spec.ts` also creates `new HomePage(page)` twice in a row.
- **The `#e2e` title tag** has no effect in this suite: only the legacy CI command filters on it. I recorded it as the current habit rather than a requirement. `feedback.spec.ts` already leaves it out.

These could be fixed or written up as exceptions.
